title: Embedding and Vector Pipelines: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Embedding and Vector Pipelines: Visual Guide

1. From Chunks To Vectors | the versioned corpus and deduplicated chunks of lessons 03-04 on one side, vector records on the other, with five tappable inputs that recompute embedding_id = hash(chunk_id, model_id, model_revision, preprocessing_version) | identity must include every input that changes the numbers, so a model or preprocessing change mints a new vector beside the old one while a permission change mints none

2. Rerun Without Duplicates | 12 chunks from 3 documents, a slider for how far the failed first run got, and three choices of write key showing what the re-run produces | keyed by the identity hash a re-run converges to 12 vectors from any starting point, keyed by document ID 9 chunks become unretrievable, keyed by an auto-generated ID the re-run appends duplicates

3. Packing The Batch | chunks of 600, 900 and 1,100 tokens fed to a 20,000-token endpoint under a fixed-count batcher versus a token-aware packer | the limit is expressed in tokens so a fixed count of 50 chunks blows it at 43,100 tokens and rejects the whole batch, while token-aware packing fills the call to a reserved ceiling and never overruns

4. Vector Plus Metadata | nine metadata fields switched on and off against five powers - filter, cite, invalidate, explain, search - plus a choice of co-located, catalog, or both | a vector without metadata cannot be filtered, cited, invalidated or explained, immutable attributes belong on the vector generation and mutable ones behind a versioned metadata stream with a metadata_version so stale payloads are detectable

5. Pre-Filter Or Post-Filter | an eligible fraction dragged from 0.05% to 50% of a 1,000,000-vector index, k of 10 or 20, and a security-versus-relevance predicate, comparing both strategies side by side | post-filtering needs k/p oversampling and returns nothing at 1% selectivity on a plain top-10 search, security predicates demand pre-filtering or partitioning inside a trusted boundary, and a 500-vector eligible subset is better served by exact scan
